subject: Archaeology
title: Pompeii's Graffiti: Ancient Social Media
description: One-minute skill: Pompeii's Graffiti: Ancient Social Media.

hook.text: Pompeii's walls are covered in over 11,000 pieces of graffiti — love notes, insults, political ads, and bar tabs.

buildup.text: One scrawl reads: 'Gaius was here.' Another says: 'I don't want to sell my husband.' Romans were just like us.

discovery.text: Election slogans cover entire walls. Candidates had their supporters paint endorsements everywhere — ancient billboards.

twist.text: Some graffiti is shockingly crude. Bathroom walls, taverns, and brothels all have messages too rude to translate here.

climax.text: This graffiti is the most honest record of Roman daily life — unfiltered, uncensored, and deeply human.

punchline.text: Romans invented social media. They just wrote it on walls.

quiz.question: Why is Pompeii's graffiti historically valuable?
options: It contains the only surviving examples of the Roman alphabet
It provides an unfiltered, uncensored record of Roman daily life
It reveals secret codes used by Roman military intelligence

details.summary: Pompeii's walls are covered with over 11,000 inscriptions — love declarations, election slogans, insults, advertisements, and crude jokes. This graffiti provides an uncensored view of ordinary Roman life far more revealing than the polished literature written by elites.
details.whyItMatters: Graffiti gives voice to people history usually ignores — workers, lovers, bartenders, and bored teenagers. It shows that human nature and self-expression have not fundamentally changed in two thousand years.
takeaways: Over 11,000 graffiti inscriptions survive on Pompeii's walls
They include love notes, insults, ads, and election propaganda
Graffiti reveals ordinary Roman voices excluded from literature

faq.question: What kinds of things did Romans write on walls?
faq.answer: Everything — from romantic messages ('I don't want to sell my husband') to obscene insults, gambling scores, election endorsements ('the pickpockets support this candidate'), philosophical musings, and advertisements for gladiator fights. The range is remarkably similar to modern social media.

faq.question: What can graffiti tell historians that literature cannot?
faq.answer: Graffiti reveals literacy levels among common people, spoken Latin versus formal written Latin, prices of goods and services, social attitudes, and personal relationships. It's unfiltered evidence of daily life that no elite author would have bothered to record.
